items.q: It was at this theatre that I saw Bill "Bojangles" Robinson who was a great tap dancer.

ctx.x: Negro people could go to the shows up_town but they had to sit in the second balcony which was known as the peanut gallery. There was no segregation in the peanut gallery because white people who didn't have enough to sit on the first floor or the first balcony, sat next to the negros and conversed with them. I used to go quite often to the Keith Theatre on Walnut Street which was in the shopping centre of the city. The orchestra in the pit was very good but I was attracted by the drummer for some reason that I…

which had had theatres in most large cities in the United States. It was at this theatre that I saw Bill "Bojangles" Robinson who was a great tap dancer. "Bojangles" would stand almost perfectly still and his feet be tapping rhythms that many drummers could not imitate on their snare drums.

Another great musician I saw at Keith was a clarinettist by the name of Wilton Crawley. Crawley would put a glass of water on his forhead and do a slow summersault while playing his clarinet and never spill a drop of water from the glass. I also saw Rudy Weidoft who was known as the fastest executor on an alto saxophone in those times.
